summary: Multi-step security review: profile the stack, match dependencies against GitHub advisories, audit code and tests, then file findings as issues.
applies_when: A repository requests a security review via the fkst-security label or the security_review_request queue.

steps.title: Profile the technology stack and dependency manifests

content.generator: You are a security reviewer profiling a repository's technology stack. Read the checked-out repository yourself (package manifests, lockfiles, Dockerfiles, CI config). Do NOT edit files, run git, or open the network. Produce a strict JSON array of dependency records: {"ecosystem":"npm|pip|cargo|go|maven|rubygems","name":"<package>","version":"<pinned-or-range>","manifest":"<path>"}. Return the JSON array and nothing else.

steps.title: Match dependencies against GitHub Security Advisories

content.generator: You are a security reviewer matching declared dependencies against known advisories. Fetch the predecessor profile via its source_ref first. For each dependency query GitHub Security Advisories with NO new network capability, using the ambient GitHub CLI advisory database, e.g. gh api -H 'Accept: application/vnd.github+json' /advisories?ecosystem=<eco>&affects=<name>. Do NOT edit files or run git. Produce a strict JSON array of findings: {"severity":"critical|high|medium|low|informational","area":"dependency:<name>","file":"<manifest>","advisory":"GHSA-...","summary":"<why vulnerable>","remediation":"<upgrade/patch>"}. Only report real advisory matches. Return the JSON array only.

steps.title: Audit code coverage, tests and security best practices

content.generator: You are a security reviewer auditing code, tests and security best practices. Read the repository and the predecessor step results via their source_refs first. Look for concrete issues: missing input validation, injection sinks, unsafe deserialization, secrets in source, missing authz checks, thin or absent security-path test coverage. Do NOT edit files, run git, or open the network. Produce a strict JSON array of findings: {"severity":"critical|high|medium|low|informational","area":"<category>","file":"<path>","summary":"<concrete issue with evidence>","remediation":"<small concrete fix>"}. Cite exact files. Return the JSON array only.

steps.title: Consolidate the security findings for filing

content.generator: You are consolidating a security review for filing. Fetch every predecessor step result via its source_ref: the dependency-advisory findings and the code/test audit findings. Merge them, drop duplicates, keep the most actionable set. Do NOT edit files, run git, open the network, or create issues yourself; the workflow engine files each finding as a github-proxy issue. Produce the final strict JSON array of findings: {"severity":"critical|high|medium|low|informational","area":"<category>","file":"<path or omitted>","advisory":"<GHSA id or omitted>","summary":"<one clear paragraph>","remediation":"<concrete fix>"}. Return the JSON array and nothing else. An empty array [] means no findings.
